aspects.says: An argument such as orElse's is evaluated before the call on every call; a Supplier overload (orElseGet, Logger.fine(Supplier)) runs the lambda only when the value is needed.
basis: section:The Method You Pass a Lambda To Decides When, How Often, and Whether It Runs

aspects.says: A lambda's stack frame is named after its enclosing method and a counter javac assigns; moving the body into a named method puts the rule's name in the trace and lets a test call it alone.
basis: section:A Long Lambda Is a Method Without a Name, and Its Stack Frame Shows It

aspects.says: A computeIfAbsent mapping function must not modify its own map; HashMap throws ConcurrentModificationException when a nested call inserts, so a memo fails only when the nested item is new.
basis: section:Spot the Problem: a Price Memo That Fails Only When a Bundle's Parts Are Unpriced

aspects.says: Incrementing a captured array slot from a parallel stream loses updates, by a different amount on each run; count() or a collector counts correctly.
basis: section:State a Lambda Changes Through an Array or a Field Is Shared by Every Invocation

aspects.says: State a lambda reaches through a captured array or a field is shared by every invocation, and a field by every call of the method; a counter kept there adds across calls or is reset by a concurrent caller.
basis: section:State a Lambda Changes Through an Array or a Field Is Shared by Every Invocation

aspects.says: A lambda captures this only when its body uses a field or an instance method without a qualifier; registered in a long-lived list, it keeps its whole object reachable, while one that uses local copies does not.
basis: section:A Lambda Keeps Its Object Alive Only When It Uses `this` or an Instance Member
